messages.subject: confidence intervals for 'projected' trajectory estimates
parts:
Hello!
My name is Ellery and I am graduate student at University of Arkansas.

I was given an old quail survey dataset to complete as a side project, and am analyzing the data using multi-season occupancy models.

I am interested in generating yearly estimates of psi for my data set. However, I am struggling to derive 95% confidence intervals for the projected estimates. 

I saw in a very old thread from 2011, "colext: how to use the predict function", that there was an example on how to do this using nonparboot methods, but I was unable to locate it. 

Any help would be greatly appreciated. Below is a copy of my code.

Thanks!
Ellery Lassiter


Here is a summary of the code:
#model
fm1<- colext(~ESHArea, ~1, ~1, ~1, umf)

# psi across years
## non-parametric bootstrap CI
## model 1-ESHAREA

npb <- nonparboot(fm1, B = 1000)
n...@projected.mean #estimates
n...@projected.mean.bsse #SE's

##attempted similar syntax as parboot
#'2' (col) as margin gives a single set of CI values, but don't align with occ or unocc estimates
apply(n...@projected.mean, 2, quantile, probs=c(0.025, 0.975))

#'c(2,1)' (rows & cols) as margin just prints the occ and unocc estimates, rather than provide CI
apply(n...@projected.mean, c(2,1), quantile, probs=c(0.025, 0.975))

##is projected.mean actually the mean? could use SE to calculate CI if so...
lower <- n...@projected.mean-npb@projected.mean.bsse
upper <- n...@projected.mean+n...@projected.mean.bsse

# empirical bayes estimate of # sites occupied in each year
## including parametric bootstrapping to get CI's
## model 1-ESHAREA
#this works :)

NumOcc <- function(fm) {
  re <- ranef(fm)
  colSums(bup(re, stat="mode"))
}

pb <- parboot(fm1, NumOcc, nsim=1000)

pb_results <- cbind(pb@t0, t(apply(p...@t.star,2,quantile,probs=c(0.025,0.975))))
colnames(pb_results) <- c("num occ sites", "lower", "upper")
pb_results 


_ _
Ellery Lassiter
Graduate Student | BISC
University of Arkansas
evla...@uark.edu

parts:
Hi Ellery,

I'm not sure why the bootstrap isn't working for you, but you might take a look at the "colext" vignette for guidance. You could also try the new posterior prediction methods that Ken recently added. Here's an example:


library(unmarked)

vignette("colext")

example("colext")

## Empirical Bayes posterior distributions
eb.post <- ranef(fm)

## Empirical Bayes posterior predictions
sitesOccupied <- predict(eb.post, func=colSums,
                         nsim=1000)

## Histogram of predictive distributions
## You could pull the mode from this
plot(table(sitesOccupied[1,])) # year 1
plot(table(sitesOccupied[2,])) # year 2

## 95% CIs for each year
quantile(sitesOccupied[1,], prob=c(0.025, 0.975))
quantile(sitesOccupied[1,], prob=c(0.025, 0.975))


Richard

parts:
Thanks for sending this along!

I was able to calculate CI's for # sites occupied using empirical bayes (second half of code I provided), it was the trajectory estimates using the 'projected' function I was having trouble with.

I'll just move forward with the empirical bayes results. Nice to have confirmation that my code and the above code arrive at the same result.

Thanks!
Ellery
